standard.title: First Nations identity and challenge
standard.description: investigate the ways First Nations Australian choreographers and/or performers celebrate and challenge multiple perspectives of Australian identity through dance
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can investigate the diversity of dance choreographed and/or performed by First Nations Australians, considering ICIP rights (Y7-8, AC9ADA8E02). They understand cultural appropriation and can apply culturally responsive approaches to First Nations dance.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students investigate the ways First Nations Australian choreographers and/or performers celebrate and challenge multiple perspectives of Australian identity through dance.

nodes.label: Celebrating and challenging Australian identity
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can investigate how First Nations Australian choreographers and/or performers use dance to celebrate and challenge perspectives of Australian identity.
nodes.minimum_width: Investigating at least one example of a First Nations Australian dance work that either celebrates or challenges a perspective of Australian identity — describing the choreographer's approach.
nodes.typical_width: Evaluating ways that First Nations Australian performers and/or choreographers work respectfully and collaboratively with communities to explore local histories, cultures and identities; investigating dance works that challenge understandings about 'first contacts' between First Nations Peoples and colonisers; exploring how choreographers and performers communicate ideas, messages and lived experiences to the broader community.
wider: Investigate a First Nations Australian choreographer's sustained practice — examining how their work has evolved in response to historical and contemporary events
Compare how two different First Nations Australian dance practitioners address Australian identity — analysing what different community positions produce in terms of choreographic choices
nodes.hinge_reason: Understanding dance as a site of cultural celebration and political challenge — not merely cultural expression — is the conceptual shift that enables genuine critical engagement with First Nations Australian art. Without it, students remain in appreciation mode rather than critical analysis.

response_modes.reason: The concept of challenging identity requires students to understand that art can be a form of advocacy, resistance and reframing — not just representation. Explore specific examples where the work explicitly challenges dominant narratives. Use resources that centre First Nations voices.
First Nations Australian choreographic practices are diverse — no single example represents the whole. Investigate multiple practitioners from different communities and contexts.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Students who investigate multiple First Nations Australian choreographic practices develop nuanced understanding of the diversity of First Nations Australian cultures and their relationships to Australian national identity — essential for informed, respectful citizenship.
success_criteria: Student can describe how a specific First Nations Australian dance work celebrates or challenges a perspective of Australian identity
Student connects the choreographer's community position and lived experience to specific choices in the work

nodes.label: Communicating lived experience through dance
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can analyse how First Nations Australian choreographers and/or performers communicate lived experiences and ideas to the broader community through dance.
nodes.minimum_width: Identifying how at least two specific choreographic choices in a First Nations Australian work communicate a lived experience or idea to a broad audience.
nodes.typical_width: Exploring the ways that First Nations Australian choreographers and/or performers use their practice to communicate ideas, messages and lived experiences to the broader community; considering how the work addresses audiences who may have no prior relationship to First Nations Australian cultures.
wider: Investigate how a First Nations Australian dance work was received by different audiences — comparing how community audiences and broader Australian audiences read the same work
Explore how a First Nations Australian choreographer's relationship to both First Nations and broader Australian cultural contexts shapes their communicative choices

response_modes.reason: Communicating lived experience is both a choreographic and a political act. Help students understand the layers of address in First Nations Australian dance — to community, to country, and to a broader national audience — and how each layer produces different interpretive demands.

success_criteria: Student identifies at least two choreographic choices in a First Nations Australian work that communicate lived experience to a broad audience
Student can explain what the work communicates and to whom — recognising that different audiences may read the work differently
